floodEvents.narrative: Areas of West Ashley flooded.  Area near Blessed Sacrament Church flooded.  St. Teresa drive and Moore drive flooded.
Portions of East Bay flooded.  Portions of crosstown flooded.  1 car stranded in high water on crosstown.
Public reported 7.5 inches of rain.  Numerous stalled vehicles in roadways being pushed to higher ground.  Intersection of Camp and Folly roads flooded.

Several hours of heavy rainfall across the county caused flooding. Highway 17 in downtown Charleston was flooded with several cars becoming submerged.  Also, the frontage road along Highway 17 in Mt.  Pleasant was closed due to high water.
Significant flooding at Charleston Naval Weapons Station.  Numerous roads flooded.  Flood waters entered one building on north side of facility.
Numerous reports of roads flooded in and near Willowbrook subdivision and along North Rhett Blvd.
Highway 61 in West Ashley flooded near 526 intersection.
Parking lot of Oakmont Apartments flooded.
2 to 3 feet of water in parking lot and across roads in Northwoods Estates.  Cars stalled in water.
Cars stranded in high water.

A narrow band of heavy rain produced significant street flooding on James Island and in the downtown and West Ashley areas of Charleston.  6.12 inches of rain was measured on James Island with radar estimates up to 8 inches.

Very heavy rainfall in a short period of time caused flooding across the Charleston Metro area. Significant flooding occurred in downtown Charleston where numerous cars were under water with many roads closed due to high water.  Sycamore Avenue in West Ashley was flooded and some roads in the Dunes West Subdivision in Mt. Pleasant were also flooded.
Heavy rainfall flooded Cainhoy road in front the Cainhoy schools.

Heavy rainfall caused flooding across the Charleston metro area. Hawthorne trailer park on Rivers Avenue in North Charleston was completely flooded with some cars under water. Many roads were flooded in downtown Charleston which caused some cars to stall out. Several roads were also flooded in the Hanahan area.
Heavy rainfall caused Turkey creek to come out of its banks onto Brookside Drive. Murray Drive and Yeamans Hall Road were also flooded.
Two cars were reported to be stranded in high water covering Medcom Road.
Water was reported covering Rivers Avenue at Otranto.
Two feet of water was reported to be covering a few subdivision side streets.

Water was reported over the road at the intersection of Cross Road and Shade Lane. Water was also reported over Chester Road and 2 feet of water was reported over the road at the intersection of Medical Plaza and University.
President Street near the Crosstown was reportedly flooded and impassable.
Two feet of water was reported over the road at the intersection of Ashley Phosphate Road and Dunlap Street. Secondary roadways were impassable.
Two and a half to three feet of water were reported over the road at the intersection of Market Street and Church Street in downtown Charleston.
Broadcast media relayed a report of water covering roads with a car starting to float near the intersection of Ashley River Road and Highway 17.

Law enforcement reported flooding near the intersection of Ashley and Fishburne Roads, President Street and Fishburne Road, Killian Road, Calhoun Street and Ogire Road, King Street and Huger Road, Bee Street between Lockwood Drive and Courtney Road, Church Street and Market Street, Franklin Street, and in the Market on Market Street.
Law Enforcement reported numerous roads flooded throughout downtown Charleston, South Carolina.
Law Enforcement reported Royal Road near Treeland Drive was flooded and impassable.
Law Enforcement reported Carner Avenue closed due to flooding. Several other roads across North Charleston, South Carolina were flooded but passable.
A trained weather spotter reported significant streen flooding on Seabrook Island, with water rising several inches above the running boards of cars.
A trained weather spotter reported the main road on Seabrook Island was impassable by most vehicles due to flooding.
The Charleston county Warning Point reported ongoing flooding on Folly Road near Camp Road in James Island, South Carolina.
Broadcast media reported flooding in downtown Charleston, South Carolina along Market Street. Portions of Market Street were blocked off by more than a foot of water covering the road.
Federal officials reported road closures along Concord Street and Hazel Street due to 6 inches of standing water in downtown Charleston, South Carolina.
Broadcast media replayed a report that 2 feet of water was inside Northwoods Mall and several cars were floating in the parking lot.

A National Weather Service employee reported a road closure along Long Point Road due to high water between the intersection of Whipple Road and the entrance to Boone Hall Plantation in Mount Pleasant, South Carolina.
A county official reported that 32 units in the Bridge Point Condominiums in Shadowmoss, South Carolina sustained some degree of damage from 2 to 10 inches of water.
The public reported that numerous roads in the Shadowmoss South Carolina subdivision were flooded and impassable.
Law enforcement reported road closures due to high water within College Park Estates along Cornell Drive, Oxford Road and Trinity Place.
A National Weather Service employee reported 1 to 2 feet of water in front of and in the back of his home in Taylor Plantation 14 miles west of North Charleston, South Carolina.

Federal officials reported that Morrison Drive in downtown Charleston, South Carolina was impassable north of the Ravenel Bridge. Two vehicles were also stranded on this road due to high water. Water up to the headlights of a vehicle was also reported along Bee Street Road.
The public reported that motorists were driving through the median due to completely flooded roads near the intersection of US 17, Orleans Road and Interstate 526.
The public reported water in numerous kitchens and garages of homes around the 15th fairway at Shadowmoss Golf Club in Shadowmoss, South Carolina.
City officials in Charleston reported that widespread flooding was occurring in downtown Charleston, South Carolina. Numerous motorists were stranded in vehicles along with several road closures.

The Broadcast Media reported water to a depth of 1 foot covering U.S. Highway 17 at the Seewee Visitors Center near Awendaw, South Carolina.
Law enforcement reported a road closure due to flooding along at Radcliffe Street and Coming Street.
Law enforcement reported a road closure due to flooding at Calhoun street and Ashley Avenue in downtown Charleston.
Law enforcement reported a road closure due to flooding along Crosstown in downtown Charleston.
Law enforcement reported 10 to 15 automobiles stalled in downtown Charleston due to flooding. At least 1 automobile had water flowing into its doors.
North Charleston Police reported Carner Avenue closed due to flash flooding between Jacksonville Road and Spruill Avenue.
Law enforcement reported a road closure due to flooding at Fishburne Street and Coming Street.
Law enforcement reported a road closure due to flooding at King Street and Huger Street.

A fire department reported roads block off by standing water along Brookside Drive and Smithfield Road.
Law enforcement reported a road closure due to flooding near the intersection of Meeting Street and Macon Street.
A county official reported portions of Coleman Boulevard closed due to flooding.

Road closures were reported along Long Point Road and in Snee Farm subdivision around marsh areas.
Law enforcement reported Bee Street impassable.

The public reported significant flooding along Indigo Fields Boulevard, with at least 1 to 1.5 feet of water covering the street, and water entering the garages of many homes.

Numerous road closures were relayed from Charleston County Law Enforcement due to heavy rainfall. Through social media, the public reported that Ashley Avenue was flooded and impassable between Sumter Street and Race Street.

Tabbuli Grill on North Market Street flooded with several inches of water inside the building. Numerous side streets near the market were flooded with a half foot of water. Flooding was also reported at East Bay and Calhoun Streets. They were not officially closed, but were impassable in spots.

Law enforcement reports that police are assisting a motorist stranded in high water.
Emergency management reports several roads closed due to flooding including Ashley Avenue at Bennett Street, parts of Morrison Drive, Market Street, and Church Street.

The following intersections were closed due to flooding including Huger and King, and Huger and Meeting.

Trinity Road flooded and impassable. Bridge completely submerged. Oxford Road was also impassable.

Public safety officials are routing traffic off of Ashley Avenue due to flooding. Report relayed through social media.

Law enforcement reported portions of Fishburne Street and Rutledge Avenue closed due to water on the roadway.

Folly Beach police dispatch reported a roadway closed due to flooding at the intersection of Center Street and West Arctic Avenue. There were also other reports of flash flooding in the downtown Folly Beach area including flood waters entering several businesses in the Center Street area.

Numerous reports of road closures due to flash flooding in and around downtown Charleston. South Market Street was closed between Meeting Street and State Street due to flooding. North Market Street was closed between East Bay Street and Meeting Street due to flooding. The roadway was closed due to flooding at the intersection of Ashley Avenue and Fishburne Street. Charleston City Police reported several road closures due to excessive rain and flash flooding.  Roads and intersections included Calhoun Street at Rutledge Avenue, Cherry Street, Ashley Avenue between Bennett and Halsey Streets, South Market Street and Church Street, and Ashley Avenue at Fishburne Street.
Elsey Drive was reported closed near the intersection with LaSalle Avenue due to flash flooding.

The combination of heavy rain and high astronomical tides led to flash flooding in Downtown Charleston. Streets included: Calhoun, Ashley, Rutledge, Bennett, Gadsden, Ogier, Vanderhourst, Spring, President, Market and East Bay.
Law enforcement on Folly Beach reported that portions of Ashley Avenue and Center Street were blocked off with barricades between 2nd East Street and 2nd West Street due to flash flooding.

The public reported 1 car flooded and a parking lot impassable at the Ashton Woods Apartments. The cost was generally estimated at 0.50K.

Several vehicles were stalled out in deep water on Coleman Blvd near the Sea Island Shopping Center.

Law enforcement reported 3 feet of water in front of a business on Old Trolley Road and that the road was closed due to flooding between Travelers Boulevard and Springview Lane. A disabled vehicle was in the road with people stuck in the waters. The cost was generally estimated to be 0.50K.
Two feet of water was reported across portions of Rivers Avenue near Interstate 526.

Berkeley County dispatch reported that Harbour Lake Road is closed between Lighthouse Drive and Pineshadow Drive. Multiple cars were flooded and water was starting to come up to buildings. Charleston City Police reported numerous roads closed due to flash flooding resulting from the heavy rainfall. These roads include Ashley Avenue, Bennett Street, President Street, Line Street, Fishburne Street , Rutledge Avenue, King Street, Huger Street, Septima Clark Parkway, and Bogard Street.

Roads closed included Batten Drive, Highway 17 near the Ponderosa neighborhood, Carolina Bay Drive near the Element at Carolina Bay Apartments and the entrance to Grand Oaks subdivision where 2 cars were also found to be stalled. Ashley Grove Apartments were also reported flooded and many homes were surrounded by water along roads that were impassable. Swift water rescues and evacuations were also reported in the Shadowmoss area.

Law enforcement and social media images indicated several road closures due to flooding in downtown Charleston. Law enforcement reports that Main Road is closed due to flooding between Highway 17 and River Road.

Law enforcement reported an estimated 3 feet of standing water at the intersection of Bears Bluff Road and Liberia Road.

A Charleston County emergency manager and law enforcement reported numerous roads closed due to flooding in downtown Charleston. Roads closed included Hasell Street between Meeting Street and Washington Street. Interstate 26 exits to Meeting Street and East Bay Street were also closed due to flooding. Water was also reported entering homes and businesses at the intersection of Tradd Street and Council Street. Swift water rescues were also being reported by broadcast media in downtown Charleston.

Law enforcement reported Waterway Boulevard closed between 21st Avenue and 24th Avenue due to flooding.

Law enforcement reported several road closures near Ladson and Hanahan. The video also depicted widespread flooding of structures in the surrounding area. The intersection of Highway 41 and Highway 402 was also reported closed due to flooding.
An emergency manager reported swift water rescues underway in the North Charleston area.

Highway 61 was flooded and closed at the intersection of Muirfield Parkway and Greenridge Road. Part of an embankment collapsed near the intersection of Interstate 526 and Dorchester Road. Water was reported entering homes along Shadowmoss Parkway and the Charleston County Swiftwater Rescue Team was deployed to Shadowmoss to evacuate a residence. Severe flooding was reported within the Charlestowne Village Mobile Home Park.  Approximately 1 to 2 feet of water was in the first floor of Dorchester Gardens Apartments and 2 to 3 feet of water was in the first floor of The Reserve At Ashley River Apartments off Dorchester Road. questions.how_often: How often does flooding happen here?
questions.home_or_car_or_stay: What should people do if flooding threatens their home or car?
questions.safety: What are the key safety measures?
questions.insurance_auto: How often does insurance pay for flooded cars?
questions.how_people_deal: How do people in Charleston-area communities live with flood risk?

answers.how_often: Use city event counts and average-per-year metrics below. These are NOAA Storm Events flood-family incidents within 20 miles of each city center.
answers.when: Use peak-month outputs from NOAA event timing. Coastal and tropical-season months are typically the highest in this region.
answers.home_or_car_or_stay: NWS guidance is explicit: never drive through flooded roads (Turn Around, Don't Drown). During active flood warning, move to higher ground and avoid walking/driving in floodwater.
answers.safety: Before: know your zone/routes and keep emergency kit. During: follow warnings, avoid floodwater, evacuate when instructed. After: avoid contaminated water and electrical hazards.
answers.insurance_auto: Best available open dataset proxy found via DuckDuckGo: the NAIC Auto Insurance Database report publishes state-level comprehensive-coverage claim frequency/loss metrics (the coverage that generally handles flood vehicle damage). It is not flood-only and not city-level, so this app treats it as context while city flood frequency comes from NOAA Storm Events.
answers.how_people_deal: Observed adaptation pattern in flood-prone communities: flood insurance uptake, elevation/mitigation projects, route planning around recurrent street flooding, and warning-driven behavior changes during heavy rain/tidal events.

evidence.source: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Bulk CSV + README
evidence.note: Event frequency/timing/damage/injury statistics are computed directly from NOAA records for 1995-2024.
Provides before/during/after guidance and Turn Around Don't Drown safety rule.
States most homeowners/renters insurance does not cover flood damage; NFIP building/contents coverage details.
Contains state-level comprehensive coverage claim metrics (frequency/loss cost), used here as the closest public payout-frequency proxy for flood-damaged vehicles.

limitations: Storm Events reports are observational and can be revised over time by NCEI.
Some records may lack coordinates; this map excludes unmappable rows.
No single open dataset provides flood-only, city-level auto insurance payout frequency; NAIC comprehensive metrics are state-level proxies.
